title: Inmate death inquest hears details behind arrest
subtitle: On July 19, 2012, an elderly man was found unresponsive in a Prince Albert prison cell before he was pronounce...
article: The six-person jury did not hear how the death occurred on the first day of what could be a five-day inquest.
However, they did hear about the circumstances preceding that on July 18, 2012 from several of 13 witnesses.
The first witness to testify was Cst. Ryan Banadyga with Prince Albert Police Service (PAPS).
He was shadowing Special Constable Tim Maier, a bylaw officer, on July 18 when he first met Ermine.
Both Maier and Banadyga testified that they encountered Ermine twice that day.
In the morning, they saw him downtown picking bottles and sober. In the afternoon, he was still downtown, but was leaning against a garbage can.

Both described him as very intoxicated, with Maier in particular familiar with the signs that Ermine was drunk. Maier was on foot patrol for two summers and testified he encountered Ermine on an almost daily basis in the downtown core, often with friends by City Hall. They became acquaintances during that time, with Maier often stopping to chat.

In addition to slurred speech, an inability to balance, the smell of liquor and an empty bottle of 20 per cent liquor nearby, Ermine's behaviour often turned from cheery while sober to irritable, according to Maier.
This included muttering obscenities.

Maier's mandate as a bylaw officer those summers was to enforce bylaws surrounding alcohol, property and occasionally parking. He testified that the Troy Cooper, the deputy chief of police at the time, mandated him to largely deal with alcohol issues which include open alcohol and intoxication in public.
In addition, Maier testified Ermine was intoxicated and elderly which led the officer to take Ermine into his police car and drive him to a detoxification unit.
Maier saw Ermine so often that he looked into his record. Through that, he found Ermine had been arrested and brought to police cells 20 times within the past 12 months.
He described that cells are only used if an intoxicated person can't be in the detoxification unit near the hospital.
Maier explained detoxification requires consent from that individual, and if their behaviour violates the detoxification standards which prohibit physical or verbal abuse they can be turned away.
In his time as an officer leading to July 18, 2012, Maier took Ermine to detoxification approximately 15 times.
At no point in that time did Ermine violate those standards, meaning he was accepted to "sleep it off" there every time.

However, on July 18, 2012, video surveillance at the detoxification unit showed officers helping Ermine onto a wheelchair. Maier described him as agitated at the time, muttering and yelling obscenities to staff and officers. At one point he swung his arms up and hit a female nurse. Although Maier did not think it was intentional, he and staff considered that behavior to be a violation of their protocols.
The jury looked at videos in that unit, in the docking bay at PAPS, and numerous locations near the PAPS prison cells.
During that video, a woman in the gallery began crying and had to leave.

Maier added that originally he was giving Ermine a ride to detoxification. But when Ermine acted abusively, Maier said it became an arrest for public intoxication under the Alcohol and Gaming Regulation Act.

Video also showed that Ermine's belt was removed in detoxification before he was taken away. As he was escorted down the prison hallway to his cell, his pants fell down to his knees and they were not picked up.
As someone not familiar with arresting people, Maier did not issue a ticket until Ermine was back in his cell.
Details of how Ermine died once he was placed in a prison cell have not yet come out in testimony.
The inquest continues throughout the week. The jury's job will be to come up with recommendations to prevent future deaths of his nature.
